title: A constraint's enforcement field is informational; the strict gate keys on severity, staleness and provenance
observation: The readiness checklist (docs/autonomous-development.md step 4) asks to move the six human-confirmed blocking constraints from `advisory_v1` to `ci` enforcement so the guard fails the commit. In the code, `enforcement` is only rendered (hunch_check_constraints output) and indexed (SQLite column); no gate reads it. isStrictBlocker (src/core/strictgate.ts) blocks on severity === blocking, not stale, and confidence >= threshold or human_confirmed provenance, so those six constraints already fail `hunch check --strict` and the CI guard on a direct scope hit. What keeps local commits advisory is the pre-commit hook's `check --staged || true`, not the field. Changing the field would change nothing observable; the lever is the hook wiring (drop `|| true` and pass --strict) or the CI guard's strictness.
evidence: grep -rn 'enforcement' src/ → only src/mcp/server.ts:987 (render) and src/store/hunchStore.ts:577 (index column) read it
src/core/strictgate.ts:31-36 isStrictBlocker(c, stale): severity blocking && !stale && (confidence >= STRICT_MIN_CONFIDENCE || human_confirmed)
